# Taken 2026-11-08 on container 1.7.1 (macOS 27.2), by asking the runtime directly and through
# opossum built from main, in two runs: the first part below, then the part after "second run".
# Repeated from the 1.6.1 captures: the wordings OPSM-412 (platform-several-no-arm64-161.txt,
# platform-several-fresh-pull-161.txt, platform-not-supported-arm64-161.txt), OPSM-502 and OPSM-217
# (network-aliases-161.txt) read, and OPSM-103, OPSM-107 and `up --wait` passing and failing. Through
# opossum, in the second run: a runtime refusal of an alias another container holds (OPSM-502, the
# run made again without it), of a service name held as an alias (OPSM-217), and `does not support`
# and `has multiple platforms` (OPSM-412). `unsupported platform` is the runtime's own answer only:
# opossum, asked for arm64 of an image with no arm64 build, got `does not support`.
# Progress lines (`[n/6] ...`) and the build's step lines are left out, the run's directory is
# written <dir>, and <dir>/opossum is written opossum. Every container, network, project, volume and
# image was named for the run and removed afterwards; the last lines of each part show none left.
#
# OPSM-201's wording was not reached: two services publishing one host port are refused first, by
# OPSM-213, so the runtime is never asked. No other wording the diagnostics read is here.

container CLI version 1.7.1 (build: release, commit: unspeci)

########## OPSM-201 / 103 / 107

$ opossum up
opossum: [OPSM-213] two entries publish host port 19532/tcp:
  - service "a" (19532:19532)
  - service "b" (19532:19532)
  give one of them a different host port.
--- rc=1

$ opossum down -v
--- rc=0

$ opossum up
warning: [OPSM-102] services "a", "b" share named volume "shared", but Apple container attaches a named volume to only one running container at a time — the others fail to start. Use a bind mount (a host path) for shared data, or bake it into the image.
Creating network v171w4-net
Starting a (alpine:3.20)
a.v171w4.opossum
Starting b (alpine:3.20)
Error: failed to bootstrap container (cause: "internalError: "failed to bootstrap container b.v171w4.opossum (cause: "unknown: "Error Domain=VZErrorDomain Code=2 "The storage device attachment is invalid." UserInfo={NSLocalizedFailure=Invalid virtual machine configuration., NSLocalizedFailureReason=The storage device attachment is invalid.}"")"")
Rolled back a — stopped and removed; nothing this `up` started is left running
opossum: [OPSM-103] service "b" can't start: Apple `container` attaches a named volume to only one running container at a time, and "v171w4_shared" (held by running container "a.v171w4.opossum") is already attached elsewhere — the second attach fails with a storage-device (VZError) error. Stop the container holding it (`container stop <name>`), or give this service its own volume; for shared data use a bind mount (a host path) instead
--- rc=1

$ opossum down -v
Removing volume v171w4_shared
--- rc=0

$ opossum up
Creating network v171w5-net
Created host directory <dir>/v171w5/notthere.conf for a bind mount
Starting m (alpine:3.20)
Error: failed to start process m.v171w5.opossum in container m.v171w5.opossum (cause: "internalError: "failed to start process (cause: "internalError: "startProcess: failed to start process: internalError: "vmexec error: mount failed with errno 20: failed to resolve '/etc/passwd' in rootfs""")"")
Nothing this `up` started is left running
opossum: starting service "m": exit status 1
  → [OPSM-107] the bind mount for /etc/passwd couldn't be resolved. If it's a config FILE, create it on the host first — opossum creates a missing bind source as a directory, which can't mount onto a file path.
--- rc=1

$ opossum down -v
--- rc=0

########## OPSM-502: an alias another container holds, through opossum

$ container run -d --name holder1.v171x1.opossum --network v171x-net,alias=cache.v171x1.opossum alpine:3.20 sleep 600
holder1.v171x1.opossum
--- rc=0

$ opossum up
Creating network v171x1-net
Starting a (alpine:3.20)
Error: alias(es) already exist: ["cache.v171x1.opossum"]
warning: [OPSM-502] service "a": network alias(es) "cache" not passed: another container already holds them. Free them, then `opossum up --force-recreate a`: where the holder is a service of this project, recreate it (`opossum up --force-recreate <that service>`); where it is a container this project no longer has, `opossum up --remove-orphans` (`opossum down` alone leaves it). A project of the same name in another directory is this project here, so these work from here too
a.v171x1.opossum
--- rc=0

$ opossum ps
SERVICE  CONTAINER         IMAGE        IP            PORTS  STATUS
a        a.v171x1.opossum  alpine:3.20  192.168.69.2  -      running
--- rc=0

$ opossum down -v
Stopping a
--- rc=0
########## OPSM-217: the service's name held as an alias, through opossum

$ container run -d --name holder2.v171x2.opossum --network v171x-net,alias=web.v171x2.opossum alpine:3.20 sleep 600
holder2.v171x2.opossum
--- rc=0

$ opossum up
Creating network v171x2-net
Starting web (alpine:3.20)
Error: hostname(s) already exist: ["web.v171x2.opossum."]
Nothing this `up` started is left running
opossum: starting service "web": exit status 1
  → [OPSM-217] another container holds this service's name as a network alias — one an earlier `opossum up` made, before a service took that name. Recreate the service that holds the alias (`opossum up --force-recreate <service>`), which no longer passes it, then `opossum up`; if the holder is a container this project no longer has, `opossum up --remove-orphans`
--- rc=1

$ opossum down -v
--- rc=0

$ container delete --force holder1.v171x1.opossum holder2.v171x2.opossum
holder1.v171x1.opossum
holder2.v171x2.opossum
--- rc=0

$ container network delete v171x-net
v171x-net
--- rc=0
